query: Earlier studies on stainless, alloy, and boiler steels reported improved hardness, wear resistance, thermal stability, or reduced mass change during aggressive salt exposure at 700–900 °C. However, these findings were specific to individual material systems and emphasized characterization or performance rather than establishing why corrosion protection persists or fails across room- and high-temperature regimes; studies combining HEAs, subsequent annealing, and hot-corrosion assessment were also reported to be minimal. For Q235 steel in its pre-exposure state, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain its corrosion-related degradation or retention of protection under these regimes? Specify a controlled study that would isolate the governing cause, predicted observations relative to an appropriate reference, the conditions under which the hypothesis should and should not apply, supporting evidence from the earlier studies, and an observation that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In Q235 steel, the intrinsic corrosion protection under aggressive salt exposures at high temperatures (700–900 °C) is governed by the quality and continuity of its native iron oxide film. Specifically, a more uniform, adherent oxide layer that forms along the pre‐existing grain boundaries delays corrosion degradation by limiting oxygen and salt ion diffusion. In contrast, areas with defective oxide coverage due to heterogeneous grain boundary distributions result in localized breakdown and accelerated corrosion.
generation.material_initial_state: Q235 steel in its pre-exposure (as-received) state with its native microstructure and minimal pre-formed protective scales
generation.intervention: Controlled annealing treatment designed to homogenize the grain boundary distribution and promote uniform in-situ oxide formation, followed by exposure to aggressive salt environments at room temperature and at 700–900 °C
generation.conditions: The hypothesis is expected to hold under conditions where temperature strongly promotes oxidation kinetics (700–900 °C) in molten salt environments (e.g., Na2SO4/NaCl mixtures). It should not apply under low-temperature/room temperature exposures where oxidation kinetics are too slow to form a protective scale over the same timescale.
generation.structural_mediator: The microstructural uniformity of grain boundaries and the continuity/coherence of the native iron oxide (e.g., Fe2O3/Fe3O4) layer that forms during exposure
generation.mechanism: At elevated temperatures, accelerated oxidation leads to the formation of a thicker oxide film. Where grain boundaries are uniformly distributed, the oxide film tends to be continuous and adherent, reducing further ionic diffusion and corrosion. However, in regions with poorly connected grain boundaries, the oxide film is defective, leading to spallation and localized accelerated corrosion. The controlled annealing intervention is proposed to enhance grain uniformity, thereby improving the oxide film quality.
generation.predicted_outcome: Annealed Q235 steel samples should exhibit a more uniform and adherent oxide film with a lower net mass gain/loss and reduced spallation compared to as-received samples when exposed to salt environments at 700–900 °C. At room temperature, both treated and untreated samples will show minimal oxide formation and similar corrosion responses.
generation.baseline: As-received Q235 steel without any annealing treatment
generation.boundary: This mechanism is expected to be significant only under high-temperature salt exposure regimes; it may not manifest at room temperature due to insufficient oxidation kinetics, nor in alloys where intentional alloying elements drastically alter the native oxide formation behavior.
generation.uncertainty: There is uncertainty in the exact oxide phase composition and adherence mechanisms on untreated Q235 steel due to the inherent variability in carbon steel microstructures. The influence of minor impurities or variations in the steel composition on the oxide film integrity is also not fully known.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two groups of Q235 steel samples: one set receives a controlled annealing treatment aimed at homogenizing the microstructure and enhancing grain boundary uniformity, while the other set remains untreated. Expose both groups to a standardized molten salt environment (e.g., 75% Na2SO4 + 25% NaCl) at 700–900 °C for a fixed period and to a room temperature control environment. Use gravimetric analysis to track mass changes over time, and perform SEM and XRD analyses to evaluate the continuity and composition of the surface oxide films and any evidence of scale spallation.
measurements: Oxide layer thickness and uniformity (via SEM imaging)
Phase composition of the oxide scale (via XRD)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the annealed Q235 steel samples do not show a statistically significant improvement in oxide layer uniformity and reduced mass change (or spallation) compared to untreated samples under high-temperature salt exposure, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Zhang et al. [] prepared a composite powder coating of TC4 and WC on the surface of TC4 titanium alloy. The results showed that adding 5%, 10%, and 15% WC content could help improve the microhardness and wear resistance of the coating, and the coating forming quality was good without cracks and other obvious defects. Chong et al. [] added 5% WC into AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy powder, and the research showed that WC enhanced the hardness of the AlCoCrFeNi coating, reduced the surface roughness, and improved the wear and corrosion resistance. Hu et al. used high-speed laser cladding to prepare a Ni/WC composite powder coating. The research showed that WC improves the microhardness and wear resistance of the coating and can refine the grain structure, and the decomposition of C and W elements precipitated from the coating played a solid solution strengthening role. Ma et al. [] studied the microstructure, microhardness, and wear resistance of a 60% WC-reinforced FeCoNiCr composite coating prepared by laser cladding. The results showed that the composite coating had good forming quality and better microhardness and wear resistance.
